key_insight: The paper shows that frontier AI agents can generate plausible-looking research follow-ups on open scientific problems, but they still fall short of meeting expert scientific standards.
engineering_relevance: For computational science teams, the result highlights both the promise of AI-assisted research drafting and the need for rigorous expert-defined evaluation before trusting agent-generated scientific claims.
method: Built the benchmark "Into the Unknown" by giving agents a science paper plus a new research direction to pursue.
Partnered with DOE national laboratory scientists to define success conditions and convert them into a rubric for each open-ended task.
Had nine frontier agents produce 15 follow-up papers each across quantum computing, plasma physics, computational chemistry, materials science, and scientific machine learning.
evidence_signal: Across 135 generated submissions, none satisfied all required conditions, and 114 failed the integrity check, often due to unsupported claims or numbers that contradicted recorded evidence.
watch_item: The benchmark is powerful but domain-specific; results may depend on how well expert-written conditions capture what counts as a valid follow-up in each field.
paper_title: Into the Unknown: Benchmarking AI agents on open scientific research problems
